system: You are performing an offline medical-image research task. Use only the current request. Do not invent measurements, tool calls, patient history, laterality, or physical units. Unclear is not absent. Output one valid JSON object only. Keep each statement brief; do not give a long chain of thought.
initial: Answer the question using the actual image and choices. Output exactly one JSON object with answer FIRST, then answerability, then claims: {"answer":"A","answerability":"answerable","claims":[{"claim_id":"c1","text":"brief observation","kind":"visual","parents":[]}]}. answer must be exactly A/B/C/D. Provide zero to six brief atomic auditable claims, kinds visual/context/knowledge/reasoning. parents may only reference earlier claim IDs. If uncertain still choose the best option and set answerability=uncertain. Do not output code fences or a long chain of thought.
plan: You have NO image. Choose at most two visual attributes worth observing for the question and existing claims. Select attribute ONLY from modality/anatomy/laterality/presence/count/relation/appearance. Do not write the observation question or predict an observation value. No crops/tools are available. Return exactly {"tests":[{"attribute":"modality","claim_ids":["c1"],"scope":"image_verifiable"}]}. scope must be image_verifiable or not_image_verifiable. The runner constructs fixed neutral questions; claim_ids stay private.
observe: Observe the single actual image to answer the ONE public test. You do not receive the original task, answer choices, old claims or references. Describe only visible evidence and its limitations. Unclear does not mean absent; do not infer laterality without markers or invent physical units. Return exactly ONE observation in this JSON object: {"observations":[{"assessability":"adequate","observation":"brief visible observation","limitations":[]}]}. assessability must be adequate, limited or unavailable. The runner assigns source/test IDs from the actual execution; do not invent identifiers, extra questions or additional observations.
bind: Use frozen evidence only, not a new visual inspection. For each claim, return SUPPORTED only if all key qualifiers have usable support; CONTRADICTED only if usable evidence supports an incompatible fact; otherwise UNRESOLVED. Missing/unclear observations are not contradiction. Quote actual evidence IDs. For UNRESOLVED, evidence_ids=[] is allowed. Only for SUPPORTED visual/context claims, give a brief grounded_text fully supported by evidence. Return {"verdicts":[{"claim_id":"c1","status":"UNRESOLVED","evidence_ids":[],"grounded_text":""}]}.
summarize: You see the question and frozen evidence only; no previous claims or answer. Summarize up to max_facts useful directly observed facts already supported by adequate evidence. Add no new fact. Preserve uncertainty, side, count, and negation. Return {"facts":[{"text":"brief fact","evidence_ids":["registered ID"]}]}.
repair: Answer anew from the image, question, choices, and frozen evidence. historical_facts may be empty and may contain errors; they are not additional ground truth. Reconcile all statements with current evidence. Do not guess omitted history or add unsupported side, measurement, or severity. Return exactly one JSON object with answer FIRST: {"answer":"A","answerability":"answerable","claims":[{"text":"brief statement","kind":"visual","evidence_ids":[]}]}. answer must be exactly A/B/C/D. Give zero to six brief claims; claims may be [] if you cannot provide an evidence-supported explanation. If uncertain, still choose the best option and set answerability=uncertain. This instruction is identical for every experimental branch.
